description:
Measured from the public causal stream (HEAD efa05d386, debug interp):

    00420: 165 DeriveRecursive evaluations over 100 functions, 65 with
    unchanged output (39% pure restart cost). Depth leaders: main/0 = 14
    evaluations, fns 208/209/213 = 10 each. Same shape on both other target
    fixtures (14/13/11/11 and 12/10 layer pyramids). Every wake is
    disposition=enqueued -- layers arrive sequentially so coalescing never
    applies.

The blocked sets of successive evaluations are literally the BFS frontiers of
the transitive call graph: main's run 1 blocks on LoweredBody(0); run 2 on 18
first-layer callees; run 3 on their FunctionDefined; ... run 13 on
LoweredBody(207); run 14 concludes. Each evaluation RE-WALKS the entire known
graph from scratch to discover one more layer -- O(depth x reachable-size) per
function -- and EVERY function repeats its own walk over the shared graph
(fns 208-215 each do 8-10 layers again).

## Fix direction

Recursion is a property of the CALL GRAPH, not of one function's private
traversal. Derive a per-function DIRECT-callees fact once (it falls out of the
lowered body), and answer Recursive(f) from cycle membership over those facts.
That makes the work proportional to edges, shared across all functions, and
incremental when one body changes. Mind
feedback_scc_inner_solver_is_tolerated_debt: prefer first-class facts over a
side-channel solver; the direct-callee fact IS the first-class form.

## Checks
- DeriveRecursive evaluations ~= number of functions (one conclusion each, plus
  bounded re-derivations on real body changes) on all three target fixtures.
- Recursive/DispatchMask conclusions unchanged (canonical program equal).
- Blocked DeriveRecursive completions drop to ~zero in the causal report.
title: DeriveRecursive is a restart pyramid: one evaluation per call-graph BFS layer
